key_insight: CHORD is a universal generative pipeline that models and synthesizes diverse 4D (3D + time) dynamics—deformations and interactions of objects—by replacing brittle, category-specific heuristics with learned, scalable choreography of object behavior.
problem_solved: Creates realistic, diverse dynamic object and scene data without handcrafted, category-specific rule engines; addresses scalability and generalization gaps in existing graphics and learning-based simulators for temporal, interacting, deformable phenomena.
method: Learn a compact 4D representation that captures object geometry, deformation, and temporal evolution so objects can be animated consistently through time.
A generative choreography module composes multi-object interactions and contact events, producing temporally coherent motion and deformation sequences conditioned on scene context or controls.
Training objectives and architectural components enforce temporal consistency, physical-plausibility priors, and compositionality so generated dynamics generalize across categories and scenes.
impact: Provides a scalable way to synthesize realistic dynamic scenes for training, evaluation, and content creation—accelerating research in 4D modeling, simulation, animation, and embodied AI by reducing reliance on manual pipeline engineering.
